title: A lead change leaves status and recorded time alone
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 3 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards", "Dana Ortiz"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Dana Ortiz") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  6. Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
    • On the Lines tab click New Line, enter a name (e.g. "Brake inspection") and labor hours (e.g. 2.0), and save the line.
    • Click the line's Approve (check) button so the work order status reads Approved.
    • As Esther Howard (second browser) click Start time clock on the line's Labor row, wait at least 1 minute, click Stop time clock, then click Start time clock again and leave it running; the work order now reads In Progress.
    • Write down the line's Actual hours (e.g. "0.02 / 2.00") and the work order's Total Hours.
  7. On the Schedule, give "Esther Howard" a shift on the work order tomorrow 8:00–12:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto Esther Howard's row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  8. If your shop locks time entries (timesheet approval), lock one of Esther Howard's entries on this work order; otherwise write 'no locked time on this site' in the result comment.
custom_steps:
1. On the Schedule, drag Esther Howard's shift on this work order to 13:00–17:00, then resize it to 13:00–16:00, then drag it onto Dana Ortiz's row.
  2. Open the work order and read Lead Technician and Status.
  3. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; in the design its button tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
  5. Drag the card from Esther Howard's column into Ralph Edwards' column and click Clear shifts if the prompt opens.
  6. Open the work order and read Status, the running clock, the line's Actual hours and Total Hours.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Moving, resizing and reassigning the shift on the Schedule does not change the lead: Lead Technician still reads Esther Howard after step 2.
  • After the lead change the Status still reads In Progress.
  • Recorded time is unchanged (Actual hours and Total Hours as written down, plus only the minutes the running clock added), Esther Howard's clock is still running, and any locked entry is unchanged.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R19, S4-R20, S4-R21, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-18 / DR-31. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R19: “Moving, resizing, or reassigning a shift on the Schedule does not change the work order’s lead technician. This is how the Schedule behaves today, and it stays that way.”
  • S4-R20: “A lead change leaves work order status unchanged.”
  • S4-R21: “Lead changes and optional shift clearing leave active, recorded, and locked time unchanged.”
